content: Cefaclor is prescribed for the treatment of specific infections caused by susceptible strains of designated microorganisms. These include: 1. Otitis Media: Cefaclor is effective in treating middle ear infections caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, staphylococci, and Streptococcus pyogenes. 2. Lower Respiratory Tract Infections: This includes pneumonia caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Streptococcus pyogenes. 3. Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis: Cefaclor is used to treat infections of the throat and tonsils caused by Streptococcus pyogenes and coagulase-negative staphylococci. 4. Skin and Skin Structure Infections: It is indicated for infections of the skin and related structures caused by Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes. Before initiating treatment, appropriate culture and susceptibility studies should be conducted to confirm that the causative organism is susceptible to cefaclor. This ensures the antibiotic is effective against the specific pathogen. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and preserve the efficacy of cefaclor and other antibacterial agents, cefaclor should only be used to treat or prevent infections that are either proven or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria. When culture and susceptibility data are available, they should guide the selection or modification of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological trends and susceptibility patterns should be considered to make an informed empirical choice of therapy.
